pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

70	- **Case score = (C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)**, clipped to 0..1. `C_open` = best opening quote; `C_best` = best package any supplier would ever accept (hidden) or your alternative.
71	- No deal scores your alternative (0 if none). **A broken must-have scores 0.** Some cases are best left without a deal.
72	- Final: each wave 0-100 (mean case score x 100); up to **500 points** over 5 waves.
73	- Category goals: `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage`, `routine`.
74	- Use `arena_kit.total_cost` to compute C for every term sheet. Formula is in `api.md`.
75	- Worked example in the brief: asking EUR 43.20/30 days, deal EUR 41.60/60 days, best 40.80/90 days gives score 0.64. A 12-month deal that covers half the need can score 0.
76	
77	## 6. Data (what the agent mines)
78	
79	Data package v1: CSV + `world.sqlite` + `facts.json` + contracts + letters/e-mails/notes. Key tables: suppliers (447),
80	parts (60), price_conditions, negotiation_history, contracts + clauses, po_lines, goods_receipts, invoices,
81	quality_notifications, scorecards, forecasts, rfqs/quotes, spend_cube, index_series/index_values (real public
82	market series), cost_drivers, should_cost, news, documents. Company "today" is **2026-09-30**.
83	
84	- Every citable fact has an ID: `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`, `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`.
85	- Reply marks each cited claim `verified`, `contradicted` (wrong figure/unknown ID, **costs trust**), `irrelevant` or `duplicate`.
86	- **True data is not automatically rewarded.** Read the supplier's situation (notes, letters, news, quote remarks) and find the trade it wants (a cash-short supplier may value payment days more than price).
87	- Some notes are noise. Sunday 08:00 release adds news, letters and a memo.
88	- Download: `uv run arena data` or `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`.
89	
90	## 7. Rules
91	
92	- **No human in the loop** during the Live Final. Start the agent before 12:00 and leave it running.
93	- The agent **must not read** `/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`, `/results` (or their JSON) during the Final. `arena board` is for humans only.
94	- One API key per team. No attacks on the service or other teams.
95	- One attempt per case in the final. Everything else counts, including weaknesses found in the bots; replays are open to the jury.
96	- Max 10 open sessions per key. Client limit ~10 calls/s.
97	- A supplier remembers only within a case.
98	- Up to **one third of hidden cases combine supplier/case types practice never shows**. Memorising practice suppliers will not work.
99	
100	## 8. Practice and tooling
101	
102	- **Quota:** 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 h (`uv run arena me` shows usage). Plan runs.
103	- Needs Python 3.12, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), git.
104	
105	```bash
106	git clone https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit.git
107	cd negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit
108	cp .env.example .env              # add ARENA_API_KEY (and the LLM provider settings)
109	uv sync --all-extras
110	uv run arena me                   # team + quota
111	uv run arena play case:P01 -v     # naive agent, one practice case; prints score + replay link
112	uv run arena data                 # download data (rerun Sun 08:00)
113	uv run arena play case:P01 --agent llm -v
114	uv run arena run --set practice --agent llm --parallel 8
115	uv run arena board                # practice leaderboard (humans only)
116	```
117	
118	- **No key yet:** `arena-sim` runs the API locally (one plain scripted supplier; teaches the API contract, not real supplier behaviour).
119	- **LLM:** `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` (needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) or `openai` for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Must answer within 60 s: use a fast model, do heavy research before opening a session. Tacto says a small cheap model is enough; reading the data matters more.
120	- **MCP server over the data:** `uv run arena mcp --data <path>` (6 read-only tools) lets Claude Code query the data.
121	- Own agent = any object with `decide(case, threads) -> {"supplier_id": ..., "message": {...}}`. Kit helpers: `total_cost`, `complete_offer`, `standard_terms`, `play`, `play_waves`.
122	- Kit's final runner: `uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10`. It waits for each wave, closes cases 90 s before the cap, and resumes after a crash.
123	
124	## 9. Submission (ehl.gg, by Sun 12:00)
125	
126	1. **Repo** with the agent and a README to run it (setup, env var names without values, command). Include the **commit hash** run in the final. Jury and tum.ai (runs a code agent over submissions) must be able to open it. **No keys in the repo.**
127	2. **Short description:** how the agent prepares, what it reads, how it decides offers, when it closes or walks.
128	3. **Slides** for the pitch (top 10 only present).
129	4. Do not push after the freeze; the top 10 are checked for it.
130	
131	**Checklist for 11:30:** final machine and network tested at the 09:00 pre-flight; `arena data` rerun after 08:00; `arena me` works; LLM credits and rate limits for ~1 h of parallel play; runner started and logging to a file; laptop on power, sleep disabled.
132	
133	## 10. Pitch
134	
135	5 min + 2 min questions. Walk the jury through one replay. Expected questions: Why did your agent write that? Would it work on a real supplier? What did it learn about suppliers, and from where? Draft jury criteria: approach, explainability, craft (not final).
136	
137	## 11. Strategy notes (from the brief's tips)
138	
139	- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; LLM picks arguments and wording.
140	- Read the supplier before arguing; read the quote PDF before accepting.
141	- Send 2-3 term sheets to learn what a supplier values; ask the roles (engineering, finance, quality) the right questions.
142	- Don't leak urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
143	- The kit's LLM agent is a **starting point, not a winner**. It only sees what the case file points to.
144	- Refuse bad accepts; fall back to a safe move if the model times out.

- Use `arena_kit.total_cost` to compute C for every term sheet. Formula is in `api.md`.
- Worked example in the brief: asking EUR 43.20/30 days, deal EUR 41.60/60 days, best 40.80/90 days gives score 0.64. A 12-month deal that covers half the need can score 0.

## 6. Data (what the agent mines)

Data package v1: CSV + `world.sqlite` + `facts.json` + contracts + letters/e-mails/notes. Key tables: suppliers (447),
parts (60), price_conditions, negotiation_history, contracts + clauses, po_lines, goods_receipts, invoices,
quality_notifications, scorecards, forecasts, rfqs/quotes, spend_cube, index_series/index_values (real public
market series), cost_drivers, should_cost, news, documents. Company "today" is **2026-09-30**.

- Every citable fact has an ID: `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`, `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`.
- Reply marks each cited claim `verified`, `contradicted` (wrong figure/unknown ID, **costs trust**), `irrelevant` or `duplicate`.
- **True data is not automatically rewarded.** Read the supplier's situation (notes, letters, news, quote remarks) and find the trade it wants (a cash-short supplier may value payment days more than price).
- Some notes are noise. Sunday 08:00 release adds news, letters and a memo.
- Download: `uv run arena data` or `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`.

## 7. Rules

- **No human in the loop** during the Live Final. Start the agent before 12:00 and leave it running.
- The agent **must not read** `/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`, `/results` (or their JSON) during the Final. `arena board` is for humans only.
- One API key per team. No attacks on the service or other teams.
- One attempt per case in the final. Everything else counts, including weaknesses found in the bots; replays are open to the jury.
- Max 10 open sessions per key. Client limit ~10 calls/s.
- A supplier remembers only within a case.
- Up to **one third of hidden cases combine supplier/case types practice never shows**. Memorising practice suppliers will not work.

## 8. Practice and tooling

- **Quota:** 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 h (`uv run arena me` shows usage). Plan runs.
- Needs Python 3.12, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), git.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit.git
cd negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit
cp .env.example .env              # add ARENA_API_KEY (and the LLM provider settings)
uv sync --all-extras
uv run arena me                   # team + quota
uv run arena play case:P01 -v     # naive agent, one practice case; prints score + replay link
uv run arena data                 # download data (rerun Sun 08:00)
uv run arena play case:P01 --agent llm -v
uv run arena run --set practice --agent llm --parallel 8
uv run arena board                # practice leaderboard (humans only)
```

- **No key yet:** `arena-sim` runs the API locally (one plain scripted supplier; teaches the API contract, not real supplier behaviour).
- **LLM:** `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` (needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) or `openai` for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Must answer within 60 s: use a fast model, do heavy research before opening a session. Tacto says a small cheap model is enough; reading the data matters more.
- **MCP server over the data:** `uv run arena mcp --data <path>` (6 read-only tools) lets Claude Code query the data.
- Own agent = any object with `decide(case, threads) -> {"supplier_id": ..., "message": {...}}`. Kit helpers: `total_cost`, `complete_offer`, `standard_terms`, `play`, `play_waves`.
- Kit's final runner: `uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10`. It waits for each wave, closes cases 90 s before the cap, and resumes after a crash.

## 9. Submission (ehl.gg, by Sun 12:00)

1. **Repo** with the agent and a README to run it (setup, env var names without values, command). Include the **commit hash** run in the final. Jury and tum.ai (runs a code agent over submissions) must be able to open it. **No keys in the repo.**
2. **Short description:** how the agent prepares, what it reads, how it decides offers, when it closes or walks.
3. **Slides** for the pitch (top 10 only present).
4. Do not push after the freeze; the top 10 are checked for it.

**Checklist for 11:30:** final machine and network tested at the 09:00 pre-flight; `arena data` rerun after 08:00; `arena me` works; LLM credits and rate limits for ~1 h of parallel play; runner started and logging to a file; laptop on power, sleep disabled.

## 10. Pitch

5 min + 2 min questions. Walk the jury through one replay. Expected questions: Why did your agent write that? Would it work on a real supplier? What did it learn about suppliers, and from where? Draft jury criteria: approach, explainability, craft (not final).

## 11. Strategy notes (from the brief's tips)

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; LLM picks arguments and wording.
- Read the supplier before arguing; read the quote PDF before accepting.
- Send 2-3 term sheets to learn what a supplier values; ask the roles (engineering, finance, quality) the right questions.
- Don't leak urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- The kit's LLM agent is a **starting point, not a winner**. It only sees what the case file points to.
- Refuse bad accepts; fall back to a safe move if the model times out.
